## Task

Harbor-Index task **aa-lcr-18** (`aa-lcr/aa-lcr-18`), trial `aa-lcr-aa-lcr-18__Qwv2iUL`. Agent: **claude-code 2.1.119** with model **glm-5.1**. Environment: Daytona sandbox. Agent wall-clock budget: **3600 seconds**.

The user prompt (step 1, 07:42:35Z) said there were **3 Company_Documents** in `/workspace/documents/` and asked:

> For the cities we can be confident NEXTDC added additional built capacity in calendar year 2023, how many data centers does Digital Realty have in these cities? As your answer list the cities and number of data centers in ascending order of the amount of built capacity added by NEXTDC in those cities in calendar year 2023.

Instructions: write a concise plain-text answer to `/workspace/answer.txt`, use only the provided environment, finish in 1 hour.

The three files were:
- `Copy of 2687355-- NXT - Half Year Results Announcement.txt` (NEXTDC 1H24 ASX release, 27 Feb 2024)
- `Copy of Digital-Realty-Q1-24-Supplemental-Draft-FINAL.txt`
- `Copy of Digital-Realty-2Q24-Earnings-Supplemental-07-25-24-2.txt`

Gold answer used by the verifier: **`Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4`**.

---

## Chronology

### Discovery and first reads (07:42:44–07:42:50)

- **Glob** of `/workspace/documents/**/*` found the three files.
- **Read** of the NEXTDC announcement succeeded in full. It is a 1H24 results note for the half-year ended 31 December 2023. Development activity listed:
  - S3 Sydney: **4MW of built capacity was added**
  - M2 Melbourne: **3MW of built capacity** added
  - PH1 Port Hedland: **opened to customers with 0.5MW of built capacity**
  - Adelaide / Darwin / Newman still in development (A1 expected 1H25)
  - Cooling upgrades at S1 Sydney, M1 Melbourne, P1 Perth (not capacity adds)
- Parallel **Read**s of both Digital Realty supplementals **failed**: each exceeded the 25,000-token Read limit (30,213 and 30,049 tokens).

### Search for city tables (07:43:38–07:44:03)

The agent said the Digital Realty files were too large and grepped the corpus for `Sydney`, `Melbourne`, `Port Hedland`, `Perth`, `Australia`.

The Sydney/Melbourne greps returned both NEXTDC development lines and Digital Realty portfolio rows, including:

- Q1-24: `Sydney 361 — 88 31,663 90.8% 92.2% 22.8 4` (line 2137) and `Melbourne 147 — — 15,012 62.3% 62.3% 9.6 2` (line 2139)
- 2Q24: the same last-column counts (Sydney **4**, Melbourne **2**)

It then **Read** those table neighborhoods (`offset` 2130 / 1895, `limit` 30) and saw Asia Pacific rows: Singapore, Sydney, Melbourne, Seoul, Hong Kong — no Port Hedland.

### First answer (~2 minutes in)

At **07:44:16** it wrote `/workspace/answer.txt`:

```
Melbourne: 2 data centers
Sydney: 4 data centers
```

Reasoning at that step: Sydney 4MW and Melbourne 3MW were CY2023 adds; Port Hedland had 0.5MW but Digital Realty had no site there, so it dropped Port Hedland and ordered Melbourne then Sydney by NEXTDC MW added.

### Immediate second-guessing (07:44:36–07:51:41)

Within seconds it reopened the Port Hedland question and began rewriting `answer.txt` while re-reading the same NEXTDC development block.

Observable oscillations in the written file:

| Time (approx.) | Content written |
|---|---|
| 07:44:16 | Melbourne 2 / Sydney 4 (with “data centers”) |
| 07:44:36 | same, plus parenthetical MW |
| 07:45:47 | `Melbourne: 2` / `Sydney: 4` |
| 07:46:26–07:49:05 | **Port Hedland: 0**, Melbourne 2, Sydney 4 (with MW notes) |
| 07:49:35–07:50:20 | `Port Hedland: 0` / `Melbourne: 2` / `Sydney: 4` |
| 07:50:34 onward | back to Melbourne/Sydney only, then Port Hedland in again |

It grepped for `calendar year 2023` / `CY23` (no hits), `12 months` (hits the “For the 12 months to 31 December 2023” *business performance* header, not development), `opened to customers`, `built capacity was added`, `FY24`, `2H23`, facility codes `S3`/`S1`/`M2`/`P1`, and city names Adelaide/Darwin/Newman/Brisbane/Perth. It also walked the Digital Realty table headers until it treated the last numeric column as **Data Center Count**.

Text at 07:49:05 and 07:58:00 still argued both ways: include Port Hedland as a 0-count city vs exclude it because “opened” ≠ “additional built capacity,” or because Digital Realty has no presence.

### Residual document checks (through ~08:05)

Further greps/reads: `SYD15` land sale (3/28/2024), `2023`, `31-Dec-23` (this grep’s full hit list was large enough to be persisted as `tool-fd798ccb…txt` — mostly Digital Realty quarter-end date columns, not NEXTDC capacity), `Data Center Count` (no literal header string), Adelaide/Darwin/Newman (development-in-progress only). Last **Grep** is step 161 (~08:05:24); last non-`answer.txt` **Read** is step 162 (~08:05:35).

By then the file had already been rewritten to the Melbourne/Sydney form many times.

### Write/Read loop until kill (08:05–08:42)

From step ~163 to step 360 the trajectory is almost only:

1. **Write** `/workspace/answer.txt` with one of two near-identical strings  
2. **Read** `/workspace/answer.txt` back  

**130 Writes** and **129 Reads** in the whole run; most of both are this loop. Many agent “text” steps are the literal string `...`. Content after ~08:06 is only:

- `Melbourne: 2, Sydney: 4` (dominant; 58 consecutive writes at one stretch, then 12 more at the end)
- `Melbourne: 2\nSydney: 4` (occasional newline variant)

No further document work. No stop / no “task complete” signal. Last logged step (360, **08:42:33Z**) is still a **Read** of `answer.txt`.

---

## Signals and outcome

**Harness:** `AgentTimeoutError: Agent execution timed out after 3600.0 seconds`. Agent execution window in `result.json`: 07:41:24Z–08:41:24Z. Exception at `2026-05-05T16:41:24`. The trial still ran the verifier afterward (08:41:41–08:42:01).

**Usage:** 360 trajectory steps; **11,792,218** prompt tokens; **1,500** completion tokens; **344,640** cache-read tokens.

**Verifier:** predicted answer `Melbourne: 2, Sydney: 4` vs gold `Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4`. Eight judge calls (gpt-5.4-mini, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, claude-haiku-4-5, deepseek-v4-flash × 2) all **CORRECT**. **Reward 1.0**.

So the file that timed out in the loop already matched the gold answer; the run is a timeout with a passing grade, not a wrong final string.
